items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Children should drink more water each day. Water helps your body stay at the right temperature. It also helps your kidneys get rid of waste.

What is the author's main point?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Water helps your kidneys

choices.label: B
choices.text: Children should drink more water each day

choices.label: C
choices.text: Your body has a temperature

choices.label: D
choices.text: Water is better than juice

items.explanation: The main point is the first sentence that states what the author wants the reader to believe or do. The other sentences are reasons that support it.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Every home should have a fire escape plan. In a fire, every second counts. Families who practice their escape plan are more likely to get out safely.

Which sentence gives a reason for why a fire escape plan is important?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Every home should have a fire escape plan

choices.label: B
choices.text: In a fire, every second counts

choices.label: C
choices.text: Fire trucks are red

choices.label: D
choices.text: Homes have many rooms

items.explanation: The sentence 'In a fire, every second counts' gives a reason why having a plan matters. It explains the urgency that makes a plan necessary.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Students should walk or bike to school instead of being driven. Walking and biking are good exercise that keeps students healthy. They also reduce traffic around the school, making drop-off time safer for everyone.

Name the two reasons the author gives to support the main point.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Walking is fun and school is nearby

choices.label: B
choices.text: Walking and biking are good exercise, and they reduce traffic near school

choices.label: C
choices.text: Students are busy and parents have cars

choices.label: D
choices.text: Exercise is important and driving is expensive

items.explanation: The passage gives two reasons: (1) walking and biking provide exercise, and (2) they reduce traffic near school. Answer B matches both reasons from the text.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Schools should have gardens where students grow vegetables. Gardening teaches students about science and where food comes from. Students who grow their own food are more likely to eat vegetables. Working in the garden also gives students time outdoors during the school day.

Which reason BEST supports the idea that school gardens help students academically?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Students get time outdoors during the school day

choices.label: B
choices.text: Students who grow food are more likely to eat vegetables

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gardening teaches students about science and where food comes from

choices.label: D
choices.text: Gardens need to be watered and weeded regularly

items.explanation: Only option C directly connects gardening to academic learning by mentioning science. The other options address health, personal habits, or garden maintenance, not academic benefits.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

People should bring reusable bags to the grocery store. Plastic bags take hundreds of years to break down and harm ocean wildlife. Reusable bags are sturdier and can carry more items without breaking. Bringing your own bag is a small habit that, when done by many people, makes a big difference.

A student says the reason about bags being sturdier does not really support the environmental main point. Is the student right?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes, because sturdy bags have nothing to do with the environment

choices.label: B
choices.text: Yes, because the main point is only about ocean wildlife

choices.label: C
choices.text: No, because sturdier bags last longer and need to be replaced less often, which reduces waste

choices.label: D
choices.text: No, because any reason about bags supports the main point

items.explanation: The sturdy bag reason does support the environmental main point indirectly: bags that last longer are replaced less often, which means fewer bags are thrown away. Option C correctly identifies this connection.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Children should learn to play a team sport. Team sports teach children how to work together toward a common goal. They help children learn to handle both winning and losing gracefully. Physical activity from sports also helps maintain a healthy weight.

Which reason connects MOST directly to skills children will use in school and in their future jobs?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Physical activity helps maintain a healthy weight

choices.label: B
choices.text: Team sports teach children to work together toward a common goal

choices.label: C
choices.text: Children learn to handle winning and losing

choices.label: D
choices.text: Team sports are fun and exciting

items.explanation: Working together toward a common goal is a skill used in school group projects and workplace teamwork. It is the most directly applicable life skill mentioned. The health reason is valuable but not specifically linked to school and career.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Cities should replace all traffic lights with roundabouts. Roundabouts reduce serious accidents because cars slow down and yield instead of running red lights at high speed. Traffic flows more smoothly through roundabouts because cars do not have to stop completely. Cities that have switched to roundabouts report saving money because roundabouts require less electricity and maintenance than traffic lights.

A city engineer disagrees with the main point and says: 'The reasons only consider benefits for drivers, not pedestrians.' Evaluate this objection. Is the engineer's concern valid?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The engineer is wrong because reducing serious accidents helps everyone, including pedestrians

choices.label: B
choices.text: The engineer is correct; the passage does not mention pedestrian safety at roundabouts, which is a real gap in the argument

choices.label: C
choices.text: The engineer is wrong because cost savings benefit everyone who pays taxes, including pedestrians

choices.label: D
choices.text: Both B and C are valid responses to the engineer's objection

items.explanation: Option D is best because the engineer's concern is both valid (B: pedestrian safety at roundabouts is not addressed) and partially addressable (C: cost savings do benefit everyone). A strong critical thinker recognizes that an argument can have a real gap and still have some counter-points. Options A and C alone are incomplete responses.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Sugar should be taxed just like cigarettes. Too much sugar causes tooth decay, obesity, and type 2 diabetes, all of which cost the health care system billions of dollars. Countries that have taxed sugary drinks have seen consumption drop significantly. If people buy less sugar, companies will make less of it, reducing its overall presence in the food supply.

Which statement BEST evaluates whether the three reasons are convincing enough to support taxing sugar?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The reasons are convincing because they cover health, real-world evidence, and economic effects

choices.label: B
choices.text: The reasons are not convincing because sugar is not as dangerous as cigarettes

choices.label: C
choices.text: The reasons are convincing because they all mention money

choices.label: D
choices.text: The reasons are not convincing because they do not include any photos or diagrams

items.explanation: Option A is correct because it identifies that the three reasons cover different types of evidence: health consequences, real-world policy results from other countries, and market effects. A well-supported argument uses varied and specific evidence, which this passage does. Option B introduces an outside comparison not in the text. Option C is inaccurate (not all reasons are about money). Option D confuses image evidence with written evidence.
